query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

AbstractHigh Entropy Alloys (HEAs) have garnered attention due to their remarkable tribological attributes. Predominantly, failure mechanisms in HEAs emanate from stress‐induced dislocations, culminating in crack propagation and film delamination. In this study, we report on the synthesis of 2D HEA of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 which facilitates shear‐induced energy dissipation at sliding interfaces. The ball‐on‐disk tribological investigations demonstrate unprecedentedly low average coefficients of friction (0.076) and wear rates (10−9 mm3 (N∙m)−1) under high contact pressures (0.936 GPa) within ambient conditions. Employing multi‐scale characterizations alongside molecular dynamic simulations, we elucidate that the presence of the HEA triggers tribocatalytic activity under high contact pressures emerging as a pivotal factor in extending lubricant lifespan during tribological tests. The resilient lubriciousness coupled with the facile spray coating methodology of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 in ambient environments paves the way for the development of a new class of solid lubricants based on 2D HEA. This deliberation has been necessitated by the imperative to address the reactivity of 2D materials across diverse environments and to ascertain their enduring stability when employed as oil additives. In this intricate backdrop, High‐Entropy Alloys (HEAs), well‐known for their robust mechanical and chemical attributes, and their ability to withstand in adverse environmental conditions, emerge as an alluring prospect.[ , , , ,  ] However, the traditional way of synthesizing HEAs in the thin film or in the bulk form includes complex routes including vacuum arc melting, spark plasma sintering, physical vapor deposition methods, and so on, which limits the ability to coat complex shapes as well as such coatings are subject to stress‐induced failure mechanism inherent to thin films limiting their overall applicability in diverse tribological systems. Our novel approach of synthesizing a transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) high entropy alloy of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 using a chemical vapor transport (CVT) process in a 2D configuration and depositing these coatings on any given substrate including complex geometries at lower cost using a solvent based spray coating process offers a game‐chang

In this study, we successfully synthesized a transition metal dichalcogenide high entropy alloy of (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 with 2D structure and tested its tribological properties by performing ball‐on‐disk friction experiments using steel against steel tribopair in an ambient environment. The lubricant was coated onto the steel substrate by the conventional air spray coating process. The lubricant displayed excellent tribological properties with low average coefficient of friction (COF) and wear rates of ≈0.076 and 2.6 × 10−9 mm3 (N∙m)−1, respectively, at the high load of 9 N (contact pressure: 0.936 GPa). The analyses performed on the wear track and wear debris indicate stress‐induced tribocatalytic activity that facilitates the self‐lubricating behavior of HEA nanoflakes during friction tests performed in ambient conditions.
